reason: This resistor ties the two differential input/drain nodes together, which reduces differential gain and is typically only used for biasing, common-mode stabilization, or test/bleeder purposes. Removing it generally improves differential behavior and doesn’t prevent the core amplifier from operating, assuming no other part of the testbench relies on that DC path.
impact_estimate: Low to moderate; may change common-mode operating point and output offset if it was providing a DC equalization path.

reason: M4 is a diode-connected PMOS load for the VOUT2 branch; deleting it still leaves the other branch (with M3) able to form a load, so the circuit can still function as an amplifier in a simplified/single-ended sense. Caveat: removing M4 makes the two sides asymmetric and VOUT2 may float or saturate unless it is otherwise loaded or clamped in the surrounding circuit/testbench.
impact_estimate: Moderate; one output node loses its pull-up/load, degrading symmetry and differential operation but not necessarily killing amplification on the remaining branch.

reason: Similarly to M4, M3 is the diode-connected PMOS load for VOUT1; removing it retains basic operation on the remaining side (with M4) if you only need one output for observation. Caveat: VOUT1 may become undefined (float/rail) without an alternate load, and overall differential balance and gain will be affected.
impact_estimate: Moderate; removes the load on one output, reducing differential functionality but allowing a simplified single-ended behavior if the other side remains loaded.
